rendering_contributiontojournal rendering_abstractportal rendering_contributiontojournal_abstractportal '' > < div class= '' textblock '' > Respiratory rate ( RR ) critical vital sign provide valuable insight various medical condition , including pneumonia . Unfortunately , manual RR counting often unreliable discontinuous . Current RR estimation algorithm either lack necessary accuracy demand extensive window size . response challenge , study introduces novel method continuously estimating RR photoplethysmogram ( PPG ) reduced window size lower processing requirement . evaluate compare classical deep learning algorithm , study leverage BIDMC CapnoBase datasets , employing Respiratory Rate Estimation ( RRest ) toolbox . optimal classical technique combination BIDMC datasets achieves mean absolute error ( MAE ) 1.9 breaths/min . Additionally , developed neural network model utilises convolutional long short-term memory layer estimate RR effectively . best-performing model , 50 % train–test split window size 7 , achieves MAE 2 breaths/min . rendering_contributiontojournal rendering_abstractportal rendering_contributiontojournal_abstractportal '' > < div class= '' textblock '' > Purpose : Physical activity ( PA ) motor competence development vital young child , yet many early childhood education care ( ECEC ) center struggle successfully implement PA program , particularly organized led educator . review aimed synthesize qualitative literature ( 1 ) identify educator-perceived barrier facilitator structured-PA ECEC center , ( 2 ) map COM-B model Theoretical Domains Framework ( TDF ) . Methods : Following PRISMA guideline , systematic search five database conducted April 2021 updated August 2022 . Records screened Covidence software using predefined eligibility criterion . Using framework synthesis method , data extraction synthesis conducted coding form Excel NVivo . Results : 2382 record identified , 35 study included , representing 2,365 educator across 268 ECEC center 10 country . Using COM-B model TDF , evidence-informed framework developed . Findings revealed greatest barrier concerned educator “ opportunity ” ( e.g . competing time priority , policy tension , indoor/outdoor space constraint ) “ capability ” ( e.g . lack PA knowledge practical , hands-on skill ) implement structured-PA . Although fewer study reported factor influenced educator “ motivation ” , several theme intersected across three COM-B component illustrating complexity behavioral determinant setting . Conclusions : Interventions grounded theory utilize system approach target multiple level influence educator behavior , flexible adaptable locally , recommended . Future work seek address societal barrier , structural challenge sector , PA educational need educator . Methods : Following PRISMA guideline , systematic search five database conducted April 2021 updated August 2022 . Records screened Covidence software using predefined eligibility criterion . Using framework synthesis method , data extraction synthesis conducted coding form Excel NVivo . Results : 2382 record identified , 35 study included , representing 2,365 educator across 268 ECEC center 10 country . Using COM-B model TDF , evidence-informed framework developed . Findings revealed greatest barrier concerned educator “ opportunity ” ( e.g . competing time priority , policy tension , indoor/outdoor space constraint ) “ capability ” ( e.g . lack PA knowledge practical , hands-on skill ) implement structured-PA . Although fewer study reported factor influenced educator “ motivation ” , several theme intersected across three COM-B component illustrating complexity behavioral determinant setting . Conclusions : Interventions grounded theory utilize system approach target multiple level influence educator behavior , flexible adaptable locally , recommended . common form pancreatic cancer , particularly lethal disease often diagnosed late refractory form treatment . Tumour hypoxia key hallmark PDAC purported contribute multiple facet disease progression treatment resistance , increased invasiveness , metabolic reprogramming , immunosuppression. < br / > Methods : used Buffa gene signature hypoxia score profile transcriptomics datasets PDAC case . performed cell-type deconvolution gene expression profiling approach compare immunological phenotype case low high hypoxia score . supported finding qPCR analysis PDAC cell line cultured hypoxic conditions. < br / > Results : First , demonstrated hypoxia score associated increased tumour grade reduced survival suggesting score correlated disease progression . reproductive-aged woman . increased adiposity pivotal severity PCOS-related symptom , treatment usually incorporates increasing energy expenditure physical activity ( PA ) . study aimed understand reason woman PCOS engage PA/exercise , could support development targeted behavioural intervention at-risk population . Validated questionnaire administered self-reported PA level , quality life , mental health , illness perception , sleep quality , capability , opportunity , motivation ( COM ) PA . Using categorical PA data , outcome compared group ; ordinal logistic regression ( OLR ) used identify whether COM could explain PA categorisation . total 333 participant eligible ; favourable difference reported body mass index , depression , mental wellbeing , self-rated health , illness perception , insomnia severity reporting highest PA level . COM score increased according PA categorisation , whilst OLR identified conscious automatic motivation explaining largest PA variance . active participant reported favourable data outcome . Patients anterior-circulation , symptomatic ICAD confirmed CT angiography ( CTA ) recruited . classified probable stroke mechanism isolated parent artery atherosclerosis occluding penetrating artery , AAE , hypoperfusion , mixed mechanism , largely based infarct topography . CTA-based computational fluid dynamic ( CFD ) model built simulate blood flow across culprit ICAD lesion . Translesional pressure ratio ( PR = Pressure /Pressure ) wall shear stress ratio ( WSSR = WSS /WSS ) calculated , reflect relative , translesional change two hemodynamic metric . Low PR ( PR ≤ median ) high WSSR ( WSSR ≥ 4th quartile ) respectively indicated large translesional pressure elevated WSS upon lesion . Among 99 symptomatic ICAD patient , 44 AAE probable stroke mechanism , 13 AAE alone 31 coexisting hypoperfusion . Excessively elevated WSS ICAD might increase risk AAE . association prominent large translesional pressure gradient . pressure cuff occlusion reactive hyperaemia flush phase 6 body site studied 51 Controls 20 SSc patient . RGB scalogram image obtained PPG , using continuous wavelet transform ( CWT ) . 2 different pre-trained convolutional neural network ( CNNs , namely , GoogLeNet EfficientNetB0 ) trained classify SSc Control group , evaluating performance using 10-fold stratified cross validation ( CV ) . classification performance ( i.e. , accuracy , sensitivity , specificity , 95 % confidence interval ) also compared traditional machine learning ( ML ) , i.e. , Linear Discriminant Analysis ( LDA ) K-Nearest Neighbour ( KNN ) . < br / > < br / > Results : participant basis DL-PPG accuracy , sensitivity specificity GoogLeNet 83.1 ( 72.3–90.9 ) , 75.0 ( 50.9–91.3 ) 86.3 ( 73.7–94.3 ) % respectively , EfficientNetB0 87.3 ( 77.2–94.0 ) , 80.0 ( 56.3–94.3 ) 90.1 ( 78.6–96.7 ) % . corresponding result ML classification using LDA 66.2 ( 53.9–77.0 ) , 65.0 ( 40.8–84.6 ) 66.7 ( 52.1–79.2 ) % respectively , KNN 76.1 ( 64.5–85.4 ) , 40.0 ( 19.1–63.9 ) , 90.2 ( 78.6–96.7 ) % respectively. < br / > < br / > Discussion : study show potential DL-PPG classification using CNNs detect SSc . rendering_contributiontojournal rendering_abstractportal rendering_contributiontojournal_abstractportal '' > < div class= '' textblock '' > Background : proof-of-concept study assessing novel approach identify patient coronary artery disease ( CAD ) using deep learning analysis bilateral-site photoplethysmography ( PPG ) waveform ( “ DL-PPG ” ) . < br / > Methodology : DL-PPG studied 37 participant ( 21 CAD ) . Scalogram ‘ spectral ’ image derived right left index finger PPG measurement collected using 3-phase protocol ( baseline , unilateral arm pressure cuff occlusion , reactive hyperaemia flush ) . Artificial Intelligence ( AI ) analysis , namely deep learning , employed scalogram image classification using Convolutional Neural Network ( CNN , “ GoogLeNet ” ) , classification performance obtained using 10-fold stratified cross validation ( CV ) . conventional machine learning ( ML ) classifier ( K-nearest neighbour , K-NN , K = 9 ) also evaluated comparison CNN deep learning methodology . Blood sample also collected giving 2 biochemical biomarkers < br / > endothelial function . Test sensitivity , specificity , accuracy , Kappa statistic determined. < br / > Results : DL-PPG sensitivity 80.9 % ( 95 % CI , 78.6–83.0 ) , specificity 87.7 % ( 85.5–89.7 ) , accuracy 83.8 % ( 82.2–85.3 ) , Kappa 0.68 ( 0.65–0.71 ) . Comparative K-NN ML performance 69.4 % ( 95 % CI , 68.7–70.1 ) , < br / > 37.5 % ( 36.7–38.2 ) , 53.9 % ( 53.3–54.4 ) , 0.069 ( 0.058–0.079 ) , respectively . difference patient control found biochemical biomarkers endothelial function. < br / > Conclusion : Substantial overall agreement found DL-PPG classification CAD angiography , DL-PPG performance clearly better conventional ML technique . deep learning classification approach , using basic pre-processing PPG pulse waveform classification , could offer significant benefit diagnosis CAD variety clinical setting needing intake body composition adult athlete . systematic review meta-analysis . Data source used PubMed , Web Science , Scopus , Taylor Francis . Eligibility criterion selecting study follows : single-group , pre-/post-Ramadan , without control group , conducted athlete aged ≥19 year training least twice week , published language August 25 , 2021 . Studies assessing dietary intake and/or body composition deemed eligible . methodological quality study assessed using QualSyst . Nine study evaluated dietary intake ; 4 rated strong quality remaining moderate . 17 selected study evaluating body composition , 7 strong quality remaining 10 rated moderate . Compared pre-Ramadan , energy ( number study , = 7 ; number participant , N = 78 ; = -0.781 ; 95 % confidence interval [ CI ] , -1.416 -0.145 ; = 0.016 ) , carbohydrate ( = 5 ; N = 50 ; = -1.643 ; 95 % CI , -2.949 -0.336 ; = 0.014 ) , water ( = 4 ; N = 39 ; = -1.081 ; 95 % CI , -1.371 -0.790 ; = 0.000 ) intake decreased Ramadan . However , fat ( = 5 ; N = 50 ; = -0.472 ; 95 % CI , -1.085 0.140 ; = 0.131 ) protein ( = 5 ; N = 60 ; = -0.574 ; 95 % CI , -1.213 -0.066 ; = 0.079 ) intake remained unchanged . Compared pre-Ramadan , body mass ( = 16 ; N = 131 ; = -0.262 ; 95 % CI , -0.427 -0.097 ; = 0.002 ) body fat percentage ( = 8 ; N = 81 ; = -0.197 ; 95 % CI , -0.355 -0.040 ; = 0.014 ) decreased fourth week Ramadan . Lean body mass change Ramadan ( = 4 ; N = 45 ; = -0.047 ; 95 % CI , -0.257 0.162 ; = 0.658 ) . Carbohydrate total water intake decreased observance Ramadan , fat protein intake unchanged . Continued training athlete Ramadan associated decreased body mass body fat percentage , lean body mass , toward end fasting month . Key pointsRamadan fasting decrease body mass body fat percentage athlete , lean body mass.Longer duration fasting could provoke pronounced decrement body mass.Carbohydrate total water intake decreased Ramadan athletes.Future study , greater methodological rigor , required better discern change dietary intake body composition Ramadan . Data source used PubMed , Web Science , Scopus , Taylor Francis . Eligibility criterion selecting study follows : single-group , pre-/post-Ramadan , without control group , conducted athlete aged ≥19 year training least twice week , published language August 25 , 2021 . Studies assessing dietary intake and/or body composition deemed eligible . methodological quality study assessed using QualSyst . Nine study evaluated dietary intake ; 4 rated strong quality remaining moderate . 17 selected study evaluating body composition , 7 strong quality remaining 10 rated moderate . Compared pre-Ramadan , energy ( number study , = 7 ; number participant , N = 78 ; = -0.781 ; 95 % confidence interval [ CI ] , -1.416 -0.145 ; = 0.016 ) , carbohydrate ( = 5 ; N = 50 ; = -1.643 ; 95 % CI , -2.949 -0.336 ; = 0.014 ) , water ( = 4 ; N = 39 ; = -1.081 ; 95 % CI , -1.371 -0.790 ; = 0.000 ) intake decreased Ramadan . However , fat ( = 5 ; N = 50 ; = -0.472 ; 95 % CI , -1.085 0.140 ; = 0.131 ) protein ( = 5 ; N = 60 ; = -0.574 ; 95 % CI , -1.213 -0.066 ; = 0.079 ) intake remained unchanged . Compared pre-Ramadan , body mass ( = 16 ; N = 131 ; = -0.262 ; 95 % CI , -0.427 -0.097 ; = 0.002 ) body fat percentage ( = 8 ; N = 81 ; = -0.197 ; 95 % CI , -0.355 -0.040 ; = 0.014 ) decreased fourth week Ramadan . Lean body mass change Ramadan ( = 4 ; N = 45 ; = -0.047 ; 95 % CI , -0.257 0.162 ; = 0.658 ) . Carbohydrate total water intake decreased observance Ramadan , fat protein intake unchanged . Continued training athlete Ramadan associated decreased body mass body fat percentage , lean body mass , toward end fasting month . Key pointsRamadan fasting decrease body mass body fat percentage athlete , lean body mass.Longer duration fasting could provoke pronounced decrement body mass.Carbohydrate total water intake decreased Ramadan athletes.Future study , greater methodological rigor , required better discern change dietary intake body composition Ramadan .
